cash_breakdown.item: Bank and cash balances - general accounts
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Private higher education group; all revenue and profit before tax were subject to contractual arrangements, 84% of assets were in those arrangements, and RMB cash conversion is subject to PRC foreign exchange controls. Education/VIE cash is therefore capped at the low end of the 0.00-0.30 default range.
cash_breakdown.reason: Only general-account cash is included in the detachable pool, and only after a severe control, dividend-path and school operating restriction haircut.

cash_breakdown.item: Restricted bank deposits securing banking facilities
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: The annual report states restricted bank deposits represented deposits securing banking facilities.
cash_breakdown.reason: Cannot be stripped without affecting secured financing.

cash_breakdown.item: Offshore foreign deposit pledged for onshore loan
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: The deposit is security for an equivalent onshore RMB loan due July 2026.
cash_breakdown.reason: Netted against paired borrowing; not counted as surplus detachable cash.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Bank and non-bank borrowings are interest-bearing financing liabilities; current and non-current borrowings are deducted at 100%.
cash_breakdown.reason: A controlling buyer must repay or assume these financing liabilities before treating cash as distributable.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Estimated from the school operating model, annual cash operating cost base and tuition/boarding services already prepaid by students.
cash_breakdown.reason: Cash needed for payroll, campus operations, semester timing and working-capital volatility is not detachable.

cash_breakdown.item: Tax, FX and dividend friction reserve
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: RMB conversion is subject to PRC foreign exchange control, and moving school/VIE cash to listed shareholders has tax and distribution friction.
cash_breakdown.reason: A conservative reserve is deducted after asset haircuts.

profit_quality.assessment: The schools convert accounting profit into operating cash flow well, but that does not make all profit distributable. The business is run through PRC private higher education entities and contractual arrangements; recent years also show recurring campus capex, land-use payments, advances to Tianping College, student prepayments and borrowings secured by tuition receivables or deposits.
adjustments: Used the 2023-2025 profit history disclosed in annual reports: RMB684.393m, RMB778.171m and RMB835.546m; median profit is RMB778.171m.
Three-year operating cash flow was RMB1,074.228m, RMB1,034.214m and RMB1,199.166m; median CFO/profit conversion was about 1.329x.
Deducted RMB350m for recurring maintenance and school-development capex needs, below the recent cash outflow for property/equipment plus land-use rights but high enough to reflect campus upkeep.
Deducted RMB50m normal working-capital and operating reinvestment reserve.

Applied a 0.45 profit haircut because education/VIE cash distribution, development fund rules, continuing capex and debt-secured tuition receivables reduce the portion realistically available to a controller.
profit_quality.cashflow_support: Operating cash flow exceeded reported profit in each of the last three disclosed years, but investing cash outflows remained large.
profit_quality.haircut_reason: Cash conversion is strong at the operating cash flow line, but distributability is constrained by PRC private school/VIE structure, development fund appropriation, campus reinvestment and debt structure.
profit_quality.cash_conversion_assessment: Strong operating cash conversion before capex; median 2023-2025 CFO/profit ratio about 1.329x.
profit_quality.maintenance_capex_assessment: Recent annual property/equipment and land-use-right cash outflows were RMB548.941m, RMB463.295m and RMB447.057m; RMB350m is used as conservative recurring maintenance/development cash need.
profit_quality.working_capital_assessment: Tuition and boarding fees are generally received in advance, but delayed-payment receivables, Tianping College advances, third-party advances and contract liabilities require a separate operating reserve.

limitations: The latest annual report found in the raw filing directory is for the year ended 2025-08-31, while the input period bucket is 2025-12-31.
Market cap is taken from rough screening input rather than an independently timestamped exchange quote.
The annual report does not split cash by listed parent, WFOE, individual schools and other VIE entities; this is handled through a severe haircut rather than treating cash as fully detachable.
Maintenance capex cannot be precisely separated from growth capex; the analysis uses a conservative recurring school-development cash need.
